results.title: BUG: Canva MCP Plugin Initialization Failure (Error -32002) on Linux Desktop App - GPT builders / Plugins / Actions builders - OpenAI Developer Community
results.content:
BUG REPORT: Canva MCP Plugin Initialization Failure on Linux Desktop App

Environment:

- OS: CachyOS (Arch Linux based) / Wayland
- App: ChatGPT Desktop Official Linux Build (Release: codex@26.930.41038 / Chromium 154)
- Package: chatgpt-desktop-bin (AUR)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open ChatGPT Desktop for Linux.
2. Invoke the Canva plugin (e.g., “Create an editable ad in Canva”).
3. Wait for the MCP app sandbox to load.

Expected Behavior:  
The Canva UI widget loads and generates the design (this works perfectly on the ChatGPT Web client with the same account).

Actual Behavior:  
The app processes for ~3.5 minutes and fails with a generic error: “Your Canva design couldn’t be generated”. [...] Technical Root Cause (Extracted from local Sentry scope\_v3.json):  
The failure is a client-side MCP tool scope and resource mismatch specific to the desktop build:

1. The client requests the widget resource and the connector returns an error:  
   `method=mcpServer/resource/read uri="ui://widget/prepare-design-generation.html" -> {"code":-32002,"message":"Unknown resource"}`
2. The sandbox guestWebContents fail to initialize with `Uncaught (in promise) [object Object]`.
3. The host rejects the widget’s tool calls:  
   `App request handling failed errorCode=-32603 errorMessage="MCP app cannot call tool outside its trusted tool scope: list-brand-kits"` (also fails for `search-designs` and `track-event-lifecycle`). [...] Note: Local network, proxy, and SSL issues were completely ruled out. The sandbox partition successfully reaches Canva’s API endpoints. This is a strict protocol contract mismatch between the desktop client’s trusted tool scope and the Canva MCP server.
